title: MEA student gathering and march for public-school improvements and student rights
location: Luanda, Angola; the reported planned concentration was at Largo do Mercado de São Paulo and intended destination was the Provincial Government; the completed route and end are unverified.
participants_original: Jornal Folha 8 reports “more than 50” MEA members gathering to protest public-school conditions and journalists’ detention. Primeiro Impacto separately reports 150 students detained during the demonstration context; detention count is not turnout.
threshold_50_evidence: Folha 8’s opened 27 April article states more than 50 MEA members were concentrating/gathering to protest poor conditions in public schools. This is an explicit attributed report above the cutoff, not an exact upper bound. It is a single report; the separate 150-detention figure in Primeiro Impacto is not used as attendance. Human review should assess reliability and any independence evidence.

title.summary: Folha 8 describes MEA members gathering to protest conditions in public schools and journalists’ detention.

start_date.summary: S002 body is dated April 26 and says the action occurred Saturday 26; S011 identifies Saturday 26 April; RTP S015 on April 24 announces the coming Saturday march. S015 is notice only.

end_date.summary: No body verifies the physical end. RTP describes a planned destination; Folha 8 describes the planned route but not its completion.

location.summary: Luanda is identified. São Paulo Market is the announced planned concentration and the Provincial Government the planned destination; the actual completed route is not verified.

scope.summary: Sources describe a student action in Luanda; no evidence of a national multi-site organized event.

organizer.summary: MEA is identified as convener/organizer; RTP advance notice names coordinator Francisco Teixeira.

demands.summary: Sources report better academic/public-school conditions, student rights and criticism of government education provision; no supplied category specifically represents education demands, so no category is forced.

participants_original.summary: Keep the claims distinct: Folha 8 reports >50 members gathering; Primeiro Impacto reports 150 student detentions in the demonstration context. The latter is not a crowd estimate.

participants_min.summary: The outlet says “more than 50” MEA members gathered, supporting a reported lower bound of 51; no maximum reported.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Opened report explicitly says more than 50 MEA members were gathering. This crosses the cutoff as attributed; corroborating independence remains unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: These accounts allege police violence and do not describe participant violence; no explicit account sufficient to code participant violence either way.

state_response.summary: Both report detentions; each reports alleged police assaults/beatings. The 150 and >50 figures are different measures and not combined. Physical dispersal, official police account, shootings and event-linked killings are unknown.

eligibility.summary: Opened contemporaneous reporting describes an executed public MEA gathering in Luanda and an attributed >50 threshold claim, with criticism/demands related to Angolan public education. Candidate remains subject to human review; source independence, route completion and precise state-target framing remain open.

notes: The event is treated as one locally reported MEA action, not one event per article or each detention. Folha 8 reports >50 MEA members gathering and includes a bylined journalist who was reportedly among detainees. Primeiro Impacto attributes a separate detention figure to an MEA spokesperson; do not convert that figure to turnout. RTP is a pre-event announcement only. No explicit written-origin link between S002 and S011 was found; their different publishers do not establish independent corroboration. No body facts from held DW, Radio Angola, Club-K, Ver Angola or Facebook results were used. Not an official MM record.
open_questions: Can an independently sourced contemporaneous account verify more than 50 people physically assembled?
Did participants complete the march to the Provincial Government, or was the event largely prevented during assembly?
What was the physical end time and did any related public action continue after April 26?
Can source origins/independence between S002 and S011 be established beyond separate publishers?
What is the exact police account, number of persons detained, injury detail, dispersal action and disposition of detained participants?
How should the education-policy demand map where the supplied category list has no education-specific category?
